title: Treasury Quarterly Refunding Announcement (May 2027), 08:30 ET
source: EST: derived, and the derivation is now anchored on a PRIMARY, MACHINE-READABLE record rather than on the loose 'first Wednesday' convention this event was proposed under. api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov/services/api/fiscal_service/v1/accounting/od/auctions_query was fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) for every non-reopened 3-Year, 10-Year and 30-Year issue settling on/about the 15th of Feb/May/Aug/Nov since 2022-11 — its `announcemt_date` field IS the refunding-announcement date, and all three tenors agree on all 16 editions. Measured against those 16: the announcement is the first Wednesday of the refunding month whenever that Wednesday falls on the 1st-5th (9 of 9, no exception); it is NOT when the first Wednesday falls on the 7th (0 of 3), and it splits when it falls on the 6th (1 of 3, the misses moving to the last Wednesday of the prior month). The first Wednesday of May 2027 is 2027-05-05 - day-of-month 5, inside the 9-of-9 band, so the alternative candidate 2027-04-28 is the tail case, not the base case. Corroborating primary: home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financing-the-government/quarterly-refunding/most-recent-quarterly-refunding-documents, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 73,519 bytes), states the current cycle in Treasury's own words - 'DOCUMENTS RELEASED at 3:00 PM Monday, august 3, 2026 ... (The next release is scheduled for November 2, 2026)' for Financing Estimates and 'DOCUMENTS RELEASED at 8:30 AM Wednesday, august 5, 2026 ... (The next release is scheduled for November 4 , 2026)' for the refunding statement. Filed estimate, and the label is about evidence rather than taxonomy: Treasury has published NO 2027 refunding date, so no primary names 2027-05-05 - it is this lane's derivation, and this lane may not self-confirm. Promotion to `TSY:`/confirmed comes when Treasury names the date, most likely in the 2027-02-03 statement. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of tic-annual-survey-final-2027-04-30 (2026-09-09); date basis re-derived and researched here 2026-09-09
notes: The May 2027 edition of the quarterly refunding: at 08:30 ET Treasury publishes the policy statement (the 3y/10y/30y refunding sizes and the forward guidance on future sizes), the TBAC report, and the auction/buyback schedules; the marketable borrowing estimates land the Monday two days earlier at 15:00 ET (proposed separately as treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03, est). Impact MEDIUM, matching the sibling treasury-refunding-2026-11-04 on the same reasoning: refunding announcements move the long end through SUPPLY rather than through the policy path, and no house playbook is macro-keyed. WHAT THE DATE BUYS, measured: the refunding announcement is a non-event once its FOMC collisions are stripped out - on the 8 of 16 editions since 2022-11 that were NOT also FOMC decision days, TLT closed 4/8 up at a mean -0.037% (permutation p=0.899) against a 50.1%/+0.003% unconditional baseline, while the 8 FOMC-collision editions ran 6/8 up at +0.715% (p=0.030). 2027-05-05 is NOT an FOMC day: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200), publishes the 2027 panel as January 26-27, March 16-17, April 27-28, June 8-9, July 27-28, September 14-15, October 26-27, December 7-8 - so the clean subset governs this edition. That is also why the DATE is the load-bearing question rather than a formality: the only alternative candidate, 2027-04-28, is the April FOMC decision day, which is precisely where the entire measured effect lives. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry. Full workup: docs/research/events/treasury-refunding-2027-05-05.md.
